Metrotown is Burnaby's downtown and its regional city centre, serving the southwest quadrant of the city. The City of Burnaby states Metrotown is the largest of its four town centres — Metrotown, Brentwood, Lougheed and Edmonds — and is designated Burnaby's downtown in the Metrotown Downtown Plan (2017).

The detached and low-rise housing sits inside that downtown plan area, in the Maywood neighbourhood. City rezoning reports place Maywood addresses on Telford Avenue, Silver Avenue, Sussex Avenue and Willingdon Avenue inside the Metrotown Downtown Plan area, south and west of the Metropolis at Metrotown core.

Maywood is described by the City as the residential heart of Metrotown, in the report for 6620 Sussex Avenue. The same report states the Maywood neighbourhood is intended to be the residential "heart" of Metrotown, with opportunities to live, gather and socialize, which is the plan role the low-rise streets around Maywood Park carry.

Silver Avenue's plan edge is Maywood Park, because the City's 2026 report for 6470 and 6508 Silver Avenue states the site is located along Silver Avenue across from Maywood Park. A house or low-rise lot on that block therefore faces a park frontage inside a High-Rise Apartment 1 designation.

The Maywood stock a house buyer actually sees is mostly older low-rise rental and strata buildings on residential-district lots, not detached houses on large lots. At 6450, 6486, 6488 and 6508 Telford Avenue, the City lists a three-storey, 33-unit strata apartment at 6450 Telford (Multiple Family Residential District RM3), a two-storey, eight-unit rental apartment at 6486 Telford (Residential District R5), a three-storey, five-unit strata apartment at 6488 Telford (RM3), and a vacant R5 lot at 6508 Telford.

The Willingdon Avenue stock is 1960s walk-up rental: the City states the site at 6622 and 6688 Willingdon Avenue is improved with two three-storey rental apartment buildings with a total of 72 units, constructed in the 1960s. The report places that site in the Maywood neighbourhood area of the Metrotown Downtown Plan.

Sussex Avenue carries the same era of stock, because the City states 6620 Sussex Avenue is improved with a 53-unit, two- to three-storey low-rise rental apartment building constructed in 1965, on five legal lots under a single civic address. Its prevailing zoning at the time of the report was RM3 Multiple Family Residential District.

Silver Avenue's current buildings are also low-rise rental, because the City's 2026 report for 6470 and 6508 Silver Avenue states the two lots are improved with low-rise residential rental buildings containing 83 rental units. Those 83 units are the existing stock on a site designated High-Rise Apartment 1 in the Official Community Plan (OCP).

blocks.text: Metrotown Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The plan that governs these streets has been partly superseded, because the City states Burnaby City Council gave final reading and adoption to the Burnaby 2050 OCP on December 9, 2025, and that supported future land use in the new OCP Land Use Map now takes precedent over individual neighbourhood-wide community plan land use maps. Where a community plan such as the Metrotown Downtown Plan does not align with the OCP, the City states the OCP is the most up-to-date direction.

Inside the plan area, designation decides what a low-rise lot can become: the City's Silver Avenue report states the 6470 and 6508 Silver Avenue site is designated High-Rise Apartment 1 within the OCP, and its current zoning is RM3 Multiple Family Residential District, with a proposed Comprehensive Development (CD) district based on the R7 High-Rise Apartment 1 District and the Metrotown Downtown Plan as guidelines. Existing zoning and plan designation are therefore two different numbers on the same Maywood lot.

Rental replacement rules shape any redevelopment of the Maywood walk-ups, because City reports for Maywood rezonings cite the Rental Use Zoning Policy (2020) and Tenant Assistance Policy (2020) among the adopted policies the proposal must align with.

Mixed-designation lots have a stated density rule: the City's Sussex Avenue report states that, per the Metrotown Downtown Plan, consolidated sites with multiple residential designations are to have their densities calculated consistently with the relative proportions of the land use designations that comprise the consolidated site. A Maywood assembly does not get the highest designation applied to the whole parcel.

blocks.text: Metrotown Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Metropolis at Metrotown is listed by the City as a Metrotown anchor, alongside the Hilton Vancouver Metrotown, Holiday Inn Express Metrotown, Element by Westin and head or corporate offices including Interfor, TELUS and Sun Life Financial. The downtown's office and hotel stock sits in the same town centre as the Maywood housing streets.

Metrotown has Burnaby's first pedestrian scramble crossing, at the intersection of Central Boulevard and the Metrotown underground parkade access, near Metrotown SkyTrain station. The City states the scramble improves safety and movement through the area, which is the main walking route between the station, the mall and the Maywood streets.

A district energy utility is planned to serve this town centre first: the City states it is creating a District Energy Utility using thermal energy from Metro Vancouver's Waste-to-Energy facility in south Burnaby, with service slated to be introduced in Metrotown and Edmonds, where almost half of Burnaby's residential growth over the next 20 years is expected.

The City has considered moving City Hall into this town centre, because Council identified Metrotown as the preferred location for a new City Hall, as it is designated Burnaby's downtown in the 2017 Metrotown Downtown Plan and a regional city centre under Metro Vancouver's Regional Growth Strategy.

Maywood Park is a plan landmark, not just a local park: the City's Silver Avenue report locates the 6470 and 6508 Silver Avenue site across from Maywood Park, and the Sussex Avenue report calls Maywood the residential heart of Metrotown. Houses and walk-ups facing Maywood Park face the neighbourhood the plan is organized around.

Growth is concentrated here by policy: the City's town centre table projects Metrotown growing from 25,800 people in 2011 to 66,800 in 2041, and from 13,300 dwelling units in 2021 to 31,800 in 2041, the largest of the four town centres. Those figures are the City's OCP projections, stated as general directions and targets.

(developer not named in the City report read); home type: 32-storey and 28-storey apartment buildings; unit count: not stated in the portion of the City report read (existing buildings on the site contain 83 rental units). Status: Planning and Development Committee on May 4, 2026 adopted a report seeking Council authorization to forward REZ #25-12 to First and Second Reading at a future Council meeting — (as of November 3, 2026).

Rezoning Reference #17-10009 — 6450, 6486, 6488 and 6508 Telford Avenue, Burnaby; applicant: Chris Dikeakos Architects Inc.; home type: high-rise market residential, retail and office building and a high-rise rental residential building; unit count: not stated in the portion of the City report read. Status: City report dated December 9, 2020 sought Council authorization to forward the application to a Public Hearing on January 26, 2021 — (as of November 3, 2026).

Rezoning Reference #21-19 — 6622 and 6688 Willingdon Avenue, Burnaby; applicant: IDS Group; home type: high-rise residential strata building with low-rise market and non-market rental components; unit count: not stated in the portion of the City report read. Status: initial City report dated June 9, 2021 — (as of November 3, 2026).

Metrotown's area-specific cost layer is redevelopment policy, because a Maywood rezoning is measured against the Rental Use Zoning Policy (2020) and the Tenant Assistance Policy (2020), both cited in City reports for Telford Avenue and Willingdon Avenue. Rental replacement and tenant assistance obligations are therefore a priced-in part of assembling a low-rise site here, not an afterthought.
That agreement is a registered cost and tenure item a buyer of that site inherits.

Metrotown Station is on the Expo Line between Patterson and Royal Oak, and TransLink's timetable lists both the Waterfront–King George and Waterfront–Production Way–University services through it. The same timetable gives Metrotown to Waterfront as 20 minutes station to station, which is the rail baseline for every Maywood street.

The town centre is served by two SkyTrain lines at the network level, because the City states its town centres have SkyTrain stations served by two lines — Expo and Millennium — and high-frequency and local bus routes. For Metrotown itself the station is an Expo Line station serving the town centre it is named for.

Walking across Central Boulevard at the station uses the pedestrian scramble, because the City states the Metrotown pedestrian scramble is at Central Boulevard and the Metrotown underground parkade access, near Metrotown SkyTrain station, and is Burnaby's first pedestrian scramble crossing. That crossing is on the route between the station and the Maywood streets south of Central Boulevard.

blocks.text: Metrotown Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the OCP designation before the community plan, because the City states the Burnaby 2050 OCP, adopted December 9, 2025, takes precedent over individual community plan land use maps where they do not align. A Metrotown Downtown Plan (2017) density figure for a Maywood lot is not the final word after that adoption.

On a consolidated Maywood site, verify the designation proportions lot by lot, because the City's Sussex Avenue report states densities on consolidated sites with multiple residential designations are calculated from the relative proportions of each designation in the site. An assembly priced on the tallest designation alone is mispriced under the plan's own rule.

For any tenanted walk-up on Telford, Sussex, Silver or Willingdon, read the Rental Use Zoning Policy and Tenant Assistance Policy before valuing redevelopment, because City reports for these streets list both as adopted policies the proposal must align with. The existing rental counts are documented in the same reports — 72 units at 6622 and 6688 Willingdon Avenue and 83 units at 6470 and 6508 Silver Avenue.

blocks.text: Metrotown home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

16 houses sold in Metrotown with a median price of $1,950,000 (the middle half sold between $1,873,250 and $2,384,500), taking a median of 28 days to sell at 92.3% of the last list price; 6% sold above list. They had a median $660 per square foot, a median year built of 1986 and a median lot of 7,326 square feet.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Metrotown?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 15 houses listed in Metrotown. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Metrotown a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: With a sales ratio of 7% in October 2026, houses in Metrotown sat in a buyers’ market. The reports read under 12% as a buyers’ market and over 20% as a sellers’ market.

faq.q: How many houses sold in Metrotown from June to October 2026?
faq.a: Between June and October 2026, 17 houses sold in Metrotown; Burnaby as a whole recorded 251.

faq.q: What did houses in Metrotown sell for?
faq.a: The median house sale in Metrotown was $1,950,000, across 16 sales from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Metrotown?
faq.a: Typical time on the market was 28 days. At the median, sale prices were 92.3% of list, and 6% of sales closed above list (November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026).
